entry.title: watch — underrated Linux command
entry.summary:
Many Linux users write small scripts to monitor system state — CPU usage, disk space, open connections, and more. The syntax is simple: watch command
By default, the command runs every 2 seconds. watch mailq
This refreshes the list of outgoing messages every two seconds so you can see the mail queue shrink or grow in real time. watch ss -tuln
This is useful when debugging network services or checking if a port becomes active. watch "ps aux | grep nginx"
This lets you observe whether a process starts, stops, or changes. You can change the refresh interval with -n. watch -n 1 mailq
This runs the command every 1 second. One of the most useful options is -d, which highlights changes between updates. watch -d netstat -tuln
This makes it much easier to see what changed since the previous refresh. watch is a small but powerful tool. It can turn almost any command into a simple real-time monitoring dashboard without writing scripts. Sometimes the best tools in Linux are also the simplest.
